articles.title: Meta introduces camera-free AI glasses
articles.summary: Meta introduced Ray-Ban Meta Audio, camera-free AI glasses that support music, calls, speech translation, and its Muse assistant, offering an alternative to smart glasses that can record people without their consent. Removing the cameras makes the frames slimmer and lighter at 43 grams, with adjustable temple tips, swappable nose pads, and a battery life of up to 12 hours. Starting at $349, the glasses come in Clubmaster and Burbank styles with prescription options.

articles.title: macOS 27 gives you more control over Liquid Glass
articles.summary: macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces a customizable Liquid Glass appearance slider that lets users adjust the system's transparency from highly clear to more opaque, changing the look of the Dock, widgets, sidebars, toolbars, and apps like Music and Podcasts with a single system-wide setting. The update gives users more control over the Mac's visual style while preserving the modern Liquid Glass design language.

articles.title: Adobe Premiere, One of the iPhone's Best Video-Editing Apps, is Now on Android
articles.summary: Adobe is bringing its redesigned Premiere video-editing app to Android, nearly a year after its iPhone debut, replacing Premiere Rush, which loses support September 30. Layouts adapt across devices, pairing footage and a multitrack timeline side by side on foldables while still running on candy-bar phones like the Pixel. The app is free with no login required, though Firefly-powered features like Generative Fill require paid generative credits once the monthly allotment runs out.

articles.title: UX-Context Design: Using UX Knowledge to Inform AI-Generated Design
articles.summary: As more interface work turns AI-generated, research and design output shifts from human-facing deliverables toward curated context that guides AI, dubbed UX-context design. DESIGN.md, which Google Labs open-sourced in April 2026 from its Stitch tool, encodes a product's visual identity for AI tools in exact values and plain-language guidance. A hypothetical broader file, UX.md, would add research findings, interaction standards, a glossary, and user and world models as a continuously updated source.

articles.title: Modernizing a legacy system? Your before/after isn't the case study
articles.summary: Strong modernization case studies focus less on before-and-after visuals and more on the design decisions behind them, highlighting the judgment calls that shaped the final product rather than the process or visual refresh alone. Employers want to understand what changed because of the designer's thinking, not just that an outdated interface now looks modern.

articles.title: Nothing has changed other than how we talk about it
articles.summary: Agentic AI can dramatically speed up the research and problem-definition phases of Design Thinking by analyzing assumptions, synthesizing evidence, and pressure-testing ideas, but human judgment remains essential for validating outputs and making design decisions. Rather than replacing designers, AI shifts their role from generating information to evaluating evidence, challenging assumptions, and deciding what should be built.

articles.title: Design Systems are a Collection of Decisions
articles.summary: Design systems amount to collections of already-made decisions, so mechanical checks can prove straight from the artifact whether an AI agent used real components and correct tokens. Judgment-based evals still have an answer key when the system has documented a decision, like a required confirmation pattern for destructive actions. Visual evals work against a known reference, but deciding whether a new visual direction deserves to exist should stay with people.

articles.title: Spatial UI Design: Tips and Best Practices
articles.summary: Augmented reality design differs from screen-based UX, demanding attention to physical space, bodily comfort, and the cognitive load added to real-world distractions. UX consultant Frank Spillers' guidelines favor real-world physics, direct hand gestures over menus, context-aware triggers, and short, interruptible interactions. Content should stay within about 30 degrees of a user's central field of view, never past 50, and sit between 1.25 and 5 meters away.

articles.title: Industrial Designer Alberto Essesi's Pen for Precision Sketching
articles.summary: Alberto Essesi's satin-finished aluminum Exclamation Pen and matching rest feature a severely tapered point that keeps the tip visible for precision sketching.
